Resp
 Prayer : Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution 
 praying for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus directing the respondent
 consider the petitioner appeal dated 26.07.2021, for re-survey and 
 fixation of compensation awarded in Roc.03/2018/LA dated :10.03.202

my lands and a well in Survey No.22/4B of an extent of 868 sq.mtrs 
 at Velagalahalli Village, Palacode, Dharmapuri District.

1/5 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

For Petitioner : Mr.P.Sharmila
Venkatachalam vs The District Collector on 1 June, 2023
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29992161/
1

 For Respondents : Mr.G.Krishnaraja
 Additional Government Plea
 Order

The relief sought for in the present writ petition is to direct the respondents to consider the appeal filed by the petitioner on 26.07.2021 to the District Collector to re-survey the acquired land and to re-fix the compensation which was awarded in Proceedings dated 10.03.2021.
2. The petitioner was owning the subject property which was acquired by the Government for expansion of National Highways.
It is not in dispute that the subject property was acquired and the road widening projects were completed.
The petitioner has already received the compensation as awarded by the competent authority.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner states that the well situated in the subject property was not measured properly and therefore the petitioner has submitted an appeal to the District Collector to re-survey the land and to re-fix the compensation.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
4. This Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner is entitled to seek an enhancement of compensation by following the procedures as contemplated under the Land Acquisition Act.
After the completion of the road widening project, question of re-measuring or re-surveying the land does not arise at all, since the project had already been completed.
This being the factum.

The petitioner is at liberty to submit a fresh application seeking enhancement of compensation by following the procedures as contemplated and in the event of receiving any such appeal from the petitioner, the District Collector may consider the same on merits and in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible.
5. With the above observations, the Writ Petition stands disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
